hints: Start by remembering what a tonoplast actually is. It is the membrane around a vacuole, so ask yourself which of these four cells has no vacuole at all.
Think about the sieve tube element and why it is so specialised for translocation. What organelles must it lose at maturity to leave a clear tube for sap flow?
walkthrough:
**Recall what a tonoplast tells us**

A tonoplast is the partially permeable membrane surrounding the vacuole.

So a cell contains a tonoplast only if it contains a vacuole. No vacuole means no tonoplast.

**Check the normal living plant cells**

Root hair cells have a large central vacuole to take up water by osmosis. Companion cells are fully living with nucleus, mitochondria and a vacuole to support the sieve tube. Endodermis cells in the root are also fully living with a vacuole.

All three of these must therefore have a tonoplast.

**Check the sieve tube element**

Mature sieve tube elements are very highly specialised. They lose their nucleus, vacuole, ribosomes and most other organelles to form an empty tube for mass flow of sucrose.

With no vacuole, there is no tonoplast. That gives tick, tick, cross, tick, which is option D.

options.A: Incorrect because it gives the sieve tube element a tonoplast. Mature sieve tube elements have no vacuole, so they cannot have a tonoplast.
options.B: Incorrect because it says the companion cell has no tonoplast. Companion cells are fully living with a vacuole, so they do have one.
options.C: Incorrect because it says root hair and endodermis cells have no tonoplast. Both are normal living cells with large vacuoles for water uptake and storage.
options.D: Correct because root hair, companion and endodermis cells all have vacuoles and tonoplasts, while the mature sieve tube element has lost its vacuole for translocation.
